match_rule: Lower-case the message, turn curly quotes into straight ones, squeeze spaces. A key word matches when it appears with no letter a to z and no digit 0 to 9 directly before or after it (other letters, such as ā, do not block a match). A skip-start or question-start counts when it is the whole message or the next character is not a to z, 0 to 9 or an apostrophe.

answers.rule: Answers to pick show only under the questions that carry them (when_shown). Under such a question the person sees its answers and can always type instead. An answer under a topic question carries the need id it gives (gives). Picking it shows that need's row at once: no key words, no model call. A question with no answers is answered by typing; the typed answer goes through the order of steps as before. Under W1 the answers are the pick labels of the matched topics, or the labels of the matched terms, at most max_at_once in list order. The topic picks show only under line TP, which shows only when the person asks what they can ask (asks_for_topics). Nothing offers topics by itself. A topic pick asks that topic's question if it was not asked yet in this visit and nothing is kept for it (keeps.use), else shows its row or plain line. A pick that holds several topics (topic_picks.holds) shows line C1 with those topics to pick. There is no answer labelled none of these: the message box is that answer.
answers.max_at_once_note: His words, 10 Nov, 20:05: let's not have more than 4. Never more than four things to pick on screen at once, anywhere. A longer list shows three and a fourth pick, More, which shows the next ones the same way. Checked by check_json.py.

answers.term_labels_note: A term label under W1 (Tools, Skills, Profile and so on) is the word the person just typed. It is not checked against R5 and R6.

when_shown.rule: A question carries answers to pick only in three cases. 1: its answer is one of a few names a newcomer may not know or may not spell (which AI, which chat app, which service). 2: it can only be answered by choosing between things Helper itself names (W1, RM2). 3: it asks for a Yes before deleting. Every other question carries none and the person types. A question with no answers must read clearly on its own.

rules: 1. From the opening: the name, and what the person does (live-v2 changes-4, his words of 11 Nov 03:58: Of course the helper still knows). The name is written at F1; what the person does is written at F2 by keeps.work. Was: what the person does is used for this visit only (tightened 19:15).

2. From the conversation: an answer to one of the three questions in answers (mod-q, msg-q, svc-q), when the person picks it, or types it while that question is the open one and code finds it by the words listed here. A new answer replaces the old one.
3. On request: what follows a request start (remember.request_starts), word for word, within remember.limits.
4. Never: anything else the person types, anything a model returns beyond rule 1, anything that matches the K1 key patterns or remember.refuse.

5. Every kept thing has a use: a question is skipped, a line is chosen, the name greets the person, or (work only) it is handed to the person's AI as one labelled line when Helper asks it (helper-talk-live-v2.json input.work_line). The name and everything else kept is never sent to any AI. In no_ai_step, work has no use yet beyond being kept and shown (changes-4, said plainly). 7. The way to see and delete everything kept ships in the same build that keeps anything: the list in the conversation (tell.see, typed). It needs no settings page.
8. At most 8 kept things in all: name, work, mod, msg, svc, and up to 3 asked. Each of the first five holds one value that is replaced, never added to.

9. Not always updating: a kept answer's question is not asked again, so it changes only through Change, through the list, or by telling Helper. Nothing is added from free typing except after a request start.

refuse.note: The K1 key patterns run first on every message. Everything kept is plain text on this computer, so a secret must not be kept even on request. The rules can miss a secret and can refuse a harmless line (rule_12, note_12).
refuse.words_note_10: Widened in changes-10: plurals and more words of the same kind. Not refused on their own, because they are ordinary words: pin (pin a chat), key (keyboard key, key point), token, secret, code, card, account. Tests: dev/checks/hhcontent-changes-10/refuse_tests.py.
rule_12: Changes-12. A secret is found by the form of what is typed, not by one word. Code: dev/checks/hhcontent-talk-v2/secret_rule.py, looks_secret(text). Used for "remember that ..." (after the K1 check, before the length check) and for every line of the settings box (on the whole line, and on the part after its first colon). The first step that matches refuses.
1. Key shapes (key_patterns) or 8 or more digits in a row (digits_pattern): refuse.

2. Lower-case the text. Cut each of not_secret_phrases (whole words), so "password manager" is not a secret word. Split into tokens on spaces; a ':' followed by a space or the end, and every '=', is a token of its own.

3. A value is a token of at least value.min_chars characters, not matching any value.not_values, that has value.digits_alone or more digits, or letters with value.digits_with_letters or more digits and value.min_chars_with_letters or more characters, or one of value.signs with a letter or digit. Examples: Riga2026, Tulip#4471, 0614, Rose_garden1. Not values: 1Password, gpt-4o, CS50x, 90, LV-1050, 7:30.
4. A secret word (secret_words, any language, whole words; or one letter off one of typo_words, such as pasword or passowrd) and a value anywhere: refuse.

5. A secret word, then within link_within tokens a link (link_words, ':' or '='), then a word that is not in after_link_not_value: refuse. So "my passphrase is correct horse ..." is refused and "my password is too short" is not.
6. A maybe word (maybe_words: pin, key, code, card ...) and a value anywhere: refuse. A maybe word alone is never refused.

7. The shape of a secret in any language: 1 to shape.max_label_words tokens, a link (link_words, ':' or '='), then exactly one token, and that token is a value. "the wifi key is GreenHouse2026", "wifi: Kafe-2024!", "mana parole ir Riga2026".
8. word_run.min_words or more words in a row that are each 3 to 8 plain letters and none of word_run.not_these: refuse (recovery words).
Anything else is not refused. A secret word or a maybe word alone is not refused: "I use Bitwarden for passwords" is kept.

steps_on_save: 1. If the whole text is longer than max_box_chars: refuse with too_much.
2. Split into lines on line breaks. Lines are numbered from 1, counting empty lines, as the person sees them. A line that is only spaces is skipped.
3. Go through the lines top to bottom. The first line that fails stops the reading; only that line is named.
4. Secret check: keeps.remember.refuse.rule_12 (looks_secret) on the whole line as typed, and again on the part after its first colon. Fails: secret_line. The line is not quoted back.
5. Take off one leading bullet: '-', '*' or the dot sign, with the spaces after it.
6. Label: the text before the FIRST colon, lower-cased, spaces squeezed to one and trimmed, must be in labels. Fails: no_label. Only a colon counts; 'Name - Pete' and 'Name Pete' fail.
7. Value: the text after the first colon, trimmed, spaces squeezed. So 'Remember: notes at 10:30' keeps '10:30'.

8. Reason: for name, mod, msg and svc, if the value ends with a bracket group '( ... )', that last group is taken off, whatever it says. For Remember, it is taken off only when its words are Helper's Remember reason (any case). A Remember value that still ends with ')' after that, and had no Helper reason taken off, fails remember_bracket.
9. Empty value after that: fails empty.
10. name, mod, msg, svc: a second line with the same label fails twice (the second line is named).
11. The value check for that label (value_rules). Fails: that label's why.
12. Remember: the same words as an earlier Remember line (any case) fail same_twice; a fourth Remember line fails too_many.
13. All lines read: the new record holds exactly what was read. Nothing else is added and told is kept as it was.

14. Forget count n = name, mod, msg, svc that were stored and are not in the new record, plus (stored Remember count minus new Remember count) when that is above 0. If n is 1 or more: ask would_delete (question_one for 1). No: nothing saved, box stays as typed. Yes: go on. The question goes away if the text is changed while it shows.
15. Write. If the new record has no values, remove the whole record, as Forget all does. Read it back and draw the box again from storage with Helper's reasons (write_rules). Show saved.

what_each_is: 1. Known key starts: OpenAI and Anthropic and OpenRouter (sk-), Stripe (sk_, rk_), xAI, Google (AIza), GitHub (ghp_ gho_ ghu_ ghs_ ghr_ github_pat_), GitLab (glpat-), Hugging Face (hf_), Groq (gsk_), Perplexity, Replicate, Fireworks, npm, Slack (xoxb- and the like, xapp-), then 16 or more letters, digits, _ or -.
2. A signed token (JWT): eyJ, two parts with a dot.
3. 32 or more letters and digits in one run, with at least one of each.
4. AWS access key: AKIA or ASIA and 16 capitals or digits.

5. AWS-style secret: exactly 40 characters of letters, digits, / and +, with a capital, a small letter and a digit, not starting with / and not touching a dot, colon or slash outside it (so web addresses and file paths do not match). wants-fixes-v1: not when the 40 characters are three or more parts joined by /, each part shaped like words: a letter, small letters, more words each a capital then small letters, digits only at the end (Projects/Club2026/AutumnSchedule/Week123 is a folder path, not a key; AWS's sample wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY is still a key).
6. A chat bot token, as Telegram gives: 6 to 12 digits, a colon, 30 or more letters, digits, _ or -.
7. The first line of a private key file.

near.about: breadth-t1: titles and phrases for every fact line, and what they are used for.
near.titles_rule: Every fact line has a title (at most eight words, a newcomer's words) and three to six phrases. The title is the only thing the person's AI sees of the line in the list call, so it names the thing the line is about, with the names that matter in it (the apps, a new computer, permission, stopping). No two titles are the same. Use 1: the person's AI is handed the list id = title and picks. Use 2, no AI: the word matching below.
near.words_rule: Words of a message or phrase: lower case, apostrophes dropped, letters digits / . + kept. A word in stop_words or filler stays as it is; any other word over 4 letters loses a final ing, else over 3 letters a final s (not ss). Filler words are dropped from the message. Content words: the words not in stop_words.
near.full_hit_rule: A phrase hits when its words are in the message in the same order side by side, or when it has two or more content words and these are side by side, in order, among the message's content words. The line with the longest hit phrase (content words, then words) wins; a tie goes to the line first in the data.
near.first_step: Stage open, the message is not a build request: a full hit by a phrase of two or more words gives that line. It runs after the small talk and before the topic list, the offer words, the topics and any AI call. It runs while things to pick are showing too: a typed message of three or more words wins over them and drops the open question. Only the new fact lines (facts_t1) and the older lines in first_step_old take part in this step: the other older lines keep their own word lists, and their phrases count at the last step and for the near offer.
near.last_step: Where Helper would say it does not know: a full hit by any phrase, one-word phrases too, gives that line instead.
near.near_rule: Still no line: show the don't-know line, and under it up to three lines near the message. A line is near when it shares two or more content words with the message (title and phrases counted), or one content word that is in its title. Most shared first; ties in data order; never the line Helper said last. The question names them by title: template (every line, a 'what Hermes can do' row too, is said by its title with a small first letter, see say_rule). A pick gives that line.
near.template: Do you want to know about {a}, or about {b}?
near.template_3: Do you want to know about {a}, {b}, or {c}?
near.template_1: Do you want to know about {a}?
near.say_rule: In the question a title starts with a small letter unless its first word is in keep_caps.
near.nothing_near_rule: Nothing near: under the don't-know line, the same four starting things to pick every time (nothing_near_picks, the four of the line TP), with the text nothing_near_text. No general question that changes. (Lead's decision, 11 Nov.)
near.never_offer_unknown: A line whose phrase is hit in full is answered, so it is never offered under a don't-know.
near.bare_follow_rule: One of bare_follow as the whole message (end marks and a leading ok / so cut), where CUT or the don't-know line would have shown: handled like 'ok and how do I do that' (small_talk.how_that): the last line's then line, next line, button, or the things to pick stay. When the last line has none of these: NO_MORE. Where an older rule already answers how / and then (after a row, after a plain line with a then line), that rule stays. Only after an answer line (a row, a plain line, a word line, a fact line, or a fixed line that has a title); after anything else CUT stays.
near.nothing_near_rule_was_t2: Nothing near: one general offer set, taken in the order nothing_near_order, skipping any set shown in Helper's last three offers. So the same general offer comes back at the earliest on the fourth don't-know, and never under a question about what Hermes is or does (those have their own lines now).
